atoms.text: Have you ever wondered where clouds come from? All clouds are made of water vapour. Clouds form when water heats up from the Sun, evaporates (turns into water vapour), rises up, and finally turns into clouds. There are three main kinds of clouds: cirrus, cumulus and stratus clouds.
atoms.sound: Have you ever wondered where clouds come from? All clouds are made of water vapour. Clouds form when water heats up from the Sun, evaporates, turns into water vapour, rises up, and finally turns into clouds. There are three main kinds of clouds: cirrus, cumulus and stratus clouds.

atoms.text: Cumulus clouds are very fluffy and have a flat bottom. You can often see cumulus clouds when it is sunny weather. However, if cumulus clouds are grey, it may rain soon.
Cirrus clouds, are another common type of cloud. These are long, thin clouds that form high in the sky.

The third most common type of cloud is the stratus cloud. Stratus clouds are very large and spread across the whole sky. They hang low in the sky close to the earth. If they are grey you can expect rain or snow. You can learn a lot about the coming weather by observing clouds. And sometimes, you can even find clouds in fun and exciting shapes!
